title: Launch Carriageway: initiative-to-sprint mapper and cross-service guardrails
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Purpose: create a repeatable, low-friction mapping from initiatives/OKRs to sprint lanes (carriageways) and release-train schedules across Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. This ticket captures the product strategy, decision criteria, and operational playbook for pairing initiatives with sprint capacity, defining guardrails (capacity, SLA windows, fallback lanes), and automating signal hooks into the release calendar.

Why now: as multiple teams prepare model/quantization runtime rollouts and console/SDK changes in Q2, we need a scalable way to: 1) translate initiative priority into sprint allocation; 2) declare cross-service dependencies early; 3) set gating criteria and rollback thresholds; and 4) produce a single source of truth for on-call and launch owners.

Scope:
- Define a small taxonomy of carriageways (QuickPatch, FeatureWave, PlatformDeep) and mapping rules for initiative cadence.
- Author a deterministic algorithm to propose sprint lane and capacity allocation given initiative size, customer impact, and SLA tolerance.
- Design a lightweight CSV/Google Sheet template and a minimal UI mock for the Console 'Launch Planner' view (staging owner, primary contacts, canary lanes).
- Establish cross-service guardrails (max concurrent high-impact launches, blackout windows, capacity escrow rules).
- Integrate signal hooks: automated calendar events, Slack alerts to #launch-ops, and telemetry links to the launch dashboard for canary metrics.
- Deliverables: PRD + acceptance criteria, CSV template + example mapping for 6 current initiatives, runbook for release-day escalation, and a small pilot with Runtime and Console teams for two upcoming launches.

Out of scope: full productized Launch Planner UI (separate initiative), deep scheduling optimization engine, and enforcement automation (we will start with advisory automation).
acceptance_criteria: A PRD describing carriageway taxonomy and deterministic mapping algorithm is published in Confluence with stakeholder sign-off
A starter CSV/Sheet template and one filled example (runtime quantization rollout) is linked in the ticket
Two pilot initiatives (one runtime, one console) complete the mapping flow and report back on capacity collisions or blockers
Clear guardrail rules documented: max 2 concurrent high-impact launches per week across runtime/console/api; blackout windows during major infra upgrades
Automated signals configured to create calendar entries and post to #launch-ops when a mapping is accepted
Runbook for launch day escalation and rollback criteria exists and has been reviewed by on-call SMEs
